As of 140 PM Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Areas of fog, some of it dense at times, will 
reduce visibilities late tonight and early Thursday morning
across the Coastal Plain and eastern Sandhills. 

Low level return moisture will continue to increase across
central NC through Thursday. Dew points this afternoon are noted
in the lower to mid 60s across the Coastal Plain and Sandhills
supporting scattered fair weather cumulus clouds. The clouds
will largely dissipate tonight but areas of fog will develop
after midnight in eastern locations and become widespread across
the southern and central Coastal Plain and the eastern
Sandhills. visibilities may drop to less than a mile in areas.
The fog should lift and burn off between 8am and 10am. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Temperatures trend well above average through 
Friday, then below normal late this weekend through the middle of 
next week.

Anomalous ridging extending from the western Atlantic will develop 
Thursday and continue through Friday, ushering in above average 
temperatures as southerly flow becomes in full swing. Generally mid 
to upper 80s Thursday will rise to the upper 80s and lower 90s on 
Friday, along with increasing humidity levels. We may get close to 
the record high in Raleigh on Thursday, but Friday's highs are 
likely to be several degrees below records as it stands now.

We continue to watch a cold front that is slated to move south and 
through the region Saturday. The ensemble and deterministic guidance 
still differ on its timing of passage, but there appears to be a 
trend of it moving through in the morning to early afternoon hours. 
With that, Saturday is a transition day. Right now, highs are 
forecast to be in the low 70s across the north, with mid 80s in the 
south. However, a faster passage would favor lower highs from what 
is presently advertised. For example, the range in max temperature 
for Raleigh from the LREF is between 73 and 84, with a mean of 78. 
The models should start to hone in on the timing in the next day or 
so, resulting in better confidence going forward.

Once the front moves through, northeast flow will bring below normal 
temperatures Sunday into the middle of next week ranging from the 
60s to low 70s, with corresponding lows Tue and Wed mornings in the 
40s to low 50s. 


KEY MESSAGE 3... Wet weather still expected Saturday and Sunday, 
which may linger into Monday, though rainfall amounts are still 
highly uncertain.

We continue to track the next weather system slated to impact 
central NC this weekend into early next week. While model and 
ensemble guidance continues to show uncertainty in its track, 
evolution, and timing, the highest rainfall chances appear to be 
focusing in on Saturday and Sunday, though a few ensemble solutions 
do indicate a low-end chance of rain lingering into early Monday. 
The bulk of the rain may hold off until Saturday night as guidance 
appears to be drier for the early part of Saturday.

Despite the better agreement on best rain chances, the overall 
rainfall totals with this event is still largely uncertain. For 
example, the latest LREF shows the range in accumulated rainfall 
between a quarter inch and 1.5 inches, with outlier solutions 
between a few tenths of an inch to 2 inches. The guidance appears to 
be struggling with at least partially on the strength or development 
of a wave of low pressure along the front and along the developing 
CAD regime Saturday night and Sunday. A more developed wave would 
trigger the higher-end of rainfall totals, while a more muted 
response would favor the low-end scenario. Convection poised to 
develop over the Gulf could also complicate matters and lead to 
uncertainty as it pertains to moisture transport across the 
southeast US.

Despite the uncertainty over the weekend, dry weather is expected 
early to middle of next week as cool high pressure is favored to 
build into the Mid-Atlantic.
